content: Now the ring itself. The five-membered azoles are the most efficient way to deliver a flat aromatic at C4, because they give the same planar ring in the same place for one atom less and far more polarity than a benzene. An oxazol-5-yl is the lightest of them: an oxygen and a nitrogen in a five-ring, no donor hydrogen of its own, and nearly two log units below benzene. The whole molecule comes to about 320 Da, which is 52 lighter than the phenyl version that produced the 0.70 and lighter even than my bromine leader. If the aryl effect is about presenting a flat ring rather than about its electron density - which is what the compact-substituent scan implied, since donors and withdrawers scored alike there - this is the most drug-like way to buy it.
